Subject: Multi-region Dedicated — replication pricing and throughput questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're narrowing in on Dedicated as the deployment shape for our production inference (global storefront personalization + fraud checks). Before we move deeper into procurement, two asks from our infra and procurement teams:

1) Architecture/pricing clarity: If we provision Dedicated capacity in two regions (us-west and us-east), do we charge per-region reserved commits (separate committed pools) or is there a single commitment that covers an active-active replicated pair?

2) Replication/DR costs: For an active-active setup with synchronous KV/embedding replication, is there an additional replication fee or egress surcharge? If we instead keep an active-passive warm standby, what pricing delta should we expect?

3) Throughput guarantees: We need firm guidance for concurrency and throughput for a 400 qps inference pattern with p95 latency target of <120ms. What pool size (A100-equivalent) do you recommend per region and what SLA commit would you attach?

I attached our draft Master Agreement (MA) for redlines — Procurement will want to see committed pricing and an optional add-on for cross-region failover testing. Can your team propose a packaging that includes: per-region commit, replication option(s), and a clear discount schedule for 12/24-month commitments?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we'd like to present to our CTO the week of 7/28.

Best,
Sarah

Subject: Re: Multi-region Dedicated — technical sizing notes for Veridian

Quick technical notes for pricing attach:

- Workload profile: 400 qps at typical prompt lengths (avg 120 tokens, peaks 400 tokens). Assuming batching + prefix cache, effective token-rate is ~48k tokens/sec across service.
- Recommendation (per region): To hit p95 <120ms at 400 qps, suggest a baseline pool equivalent of 6 x A100-80GB-class slots (sustained). That maps to ~2,400 concurrent model contexts with our batching engine and KV cache.
- Active-Active (synchronous replication): requires cross-region KV replication and double-write line on embeddings for consistency — overhead approx +12–18% CPU/GPU cycles (network bound). Operationally, Active-Active gives near-zero RTO but increases sustained resource usage.
- Active-Passive warm standby: keep a warm pool (30% capacity of primary) plus snapshot/async replication; failover adds an RTO (few minutes) but steady-state cost is cheaper (~40% of dual active cost).
- Failover testing: recommend scheduled run once per quarter; we can offer a 2% monthly credit for documented test windows if included in contract.

I'll drop a spreadsheet with line-itemized hourly-equivalent pricing and replication overheads — Rishi, please slot the discount tiers here.

— Dev

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 18 Jul 2025 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-region Dedicated — proposed pricing matrix (internal)

Attaching the internal pricing sheet I just finished (RI_multi-region-pricing-v2.xlsx). Key commercial terms to propose:

Option A — Active-Active (per-region reserved commits, replicated):
- Commit: 2 x 6-slot pools (us-west + us-east)
- Base list: $90k/month per region (6-slot equivalent), total $180k/month
- Replication surcharge (network + replication overhead): +12% on committed base when synchronous active-active (+$21.6k/month)
- 12-month commit discount: 18% off base list (pre-surcharge). 24-month commit: 28% off base list.
- Resulting 24-month all-in estimate: ~$230k/month (post-discount + replication surcharge)

Option B — Active-Passive warm standby:
- Commit: 1 x 6-slot primary + 1 x 2-slot warm standby (30% capacity)
- Base list: $90k/month + $30k/month = $120k/month
- Asynchronous replication surcharge: +6%
- 12-month discount: 15%; 24-month: 24%
- Resulting 24-month all-in estimate: ~$96k/month (post-discount + replication surcharge)

Other commercial notes:
- Cross-region egress: we absorb standard cross-region control-plane traffic; large bulk embedding sync (if chosen) will be billed at cost with a 5% admin margin — callout in contract.
- Failover test credit: one-time 2% credit on next invoice for quarterly documented run (as Dev suggested).
- Volume credits: if Veridian increases committed slots across regions within 90 days, we can offer a retroactive uplift to the higher discount tier.

I recommend we present both options and highlight the tradeoff between cost and RTO. Kimberly — happy to join a call with Sarah and Amit to walk through numbers.

— Rishi

Subject: Pricing options and next steps — Veridian Dedicated (summary)

Hi Sarah / Amit — thanks for the patience. Please find below a concise summary and our recommended path forward. I attached the detailed pricing workbook and a draft failover playbook for your legal/ops review.

Executive summary (two options):

1) Active-Active (recommended if you require near-zero RTO):
- Architecture: Dedicated 6-slot pools in us-west and us-east, synchronous replication for KV/embeddings.
- Commercial: list $180k/month; 24-month committed net ~ $230k/month (includes replication surcharge after discount).
- Pros: instant failover, no cold-starting models, consistent latency.
- Cons: higher steady-state cost (+12–18% compute overhead).

2) Active-Passive (recommended cost-first):
- Architecture: Dedicated 6-slot primary + warm 2-slot standby; async replication.
- Commercial: list $120k/month; 24-month committed net ~ $96k/month after discounts and surcharge.
- Pros: material cost savings, simpler replication needs.
- Cons: RTO measured in minutes for high-traffic failover windows.

Contract/logistics notes:
- We propose a 24-month committed term to secure the best pricing.
- Cross-region embedding bulk sync will be billed at-cost + 5% admin margin (will call out in SOW).
- We will include two failover test windows per year; each documented test grants a 2% invoice credit toward the next billing cycle.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm target RTO ceiling (minutes vs seconds) and whether procurement needs us to waive the egress admin margin?
- If you want to proceed with Active-Active, we will prepare a redline-friendly SOW + MSA update specific to replication/DR pricing.
- If you prefer Active-Passive, we can prepare an addendum that defines warm standby sizing and testing cadence.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call Tues 7/22 or Wed 7/23 to finalize which path you'd like us to formalize?

Thanks — kim

Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
